A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same underlying research, despite substantial retitling and narrowing of scope. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching.

before.justification: v2 Section 9 reports original classifier evaluations, fairness-bound calculations and data analyses, including Census, Natality, cancer, election, Adult and COMPAS experiments.

after.justification: v3 Section 7 and Appendices A–B report original multiclass evaluations and data analyses. Appendix D additionally reports an optimization convergence experiment.

M1.justification: v3 removes the general accuracy–fairness trade-off procedure, the fair-classifier error minimization program and the explicit binary discrepancy solver from v2 Sections 5 and 8. The retained multiclass mixture measure, greedy initialization and sequential linear programming remain substantially the same: DCP corresponds to unfairness, and minDCP to mindisc1.

E1.justification: v3 removes binary Census prediction tasks, Adult income and COMPAS recidivism evaluations, cancer diagnosis/mortality applications and US presidential-poll analyses. Multiclass Census, Natality, UK elections and US education remain; education moves to Appendix B. Added neural-network evaluations use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: The multiclass comparisons retain Average, Greedy, Average+LM and Greedy+LM in both versions. The new neural networks are classifiers being audited, rather than additional fairness-estimation baselines. No other evaluated competing estimation method is added or removed.

E3.justification: The binary evaluation protocols, including Census's random half-training/half-test split, beta sweeps and class-weight controls, disappear. v3 adds neural-network configurations, including Census networks trained for four epochs with AdamW, and a convergence experiment varying maximum steps from 0.025 to 0.2 under a substitute objective. Changed Census scores do not establish a change to the retained experiments' splits.

E4.justification: v2's beta-sensitivity and Pareto analyses, cancer association studies, and Adult/COMPAS investigations of weak bounds with few sub-populations are removed. v3 Appendix D adds a step-size/convergence analysis on Natality using a substitute eta function. The existing greedy-initialization/local-minimization comparisons remain.

E5.justification: The correlation-based statistical reporting in v2 Figures 11–12, relating unfairness to care costs and survival, disappears. Both versions retain ten random label orderings for greedy initialization and provide no benchmark confidence intervals or repeated-run variability estimates. The reported optimization bounds are not statistical confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Binary results are removed, Census results are extensively replaced, and neural-network results are added in v3 Tables 5–8. For example, the eight-label Census decision tree changes from 22.36% error and a 19.74% Greedy+LM upper bound to 22.61% and 23.61%; this does not establish a same-setting performance change. Natality bounding results, UK-election values and education values remain, although Natality's reported nearest-neighbor error changes from 24.26% to 24.6%.

T1.justification: v3 removes the discrepancy trade-off formalism, binary reduction theorem, Lipschitz analysis and supporting proofs in v2 Appendices A–B. The retained multiclass derivation gains an explicit nuisance-distribution simplex argument in Theorem 4.1. Appendix D adds a substitute eta definition and convergence reasoning, rather than a new proof of convergence for the original DCP objective.

C1.justification: The contribution changes from quantifying and bounding fairness, accuracy and their trade-offs in binary and multiclass classification to extending binary DCP and estimating multiclass DCP in two information regimes. v3 abandons the claim of introducing multiclass equalized odds and foregrounds claims of accurate estimation in both regimes.

C2.justification: v3 removes detailed interpretations of cancer disparities, classifier-type differences and failures with few sub-populations. It adds the assertion that distribution-estimation error transfers to DCP without amplification, discusses step-size-dependent local minima, and introduces guidance about fairness-criterion suitability and caution when bounds are loose. These change substantive applicability and reliability interpretations.

D1.justification: Detailed binary data-processing and classifier-construction instructions disappear. v3 documents neural-network architecture, PyTorch, AdamW, learning rate, batch size and training epochs, and newly specifies tau=0.2 with reductions after LP failures. The code pointer changes from sivansabato/unfairness to sivansabato/DCPmulticlass. These disclosures do not establish that previously unspecified solver settings changed.

R1.justification: v3 replaces v2's assertion that prior multiclass equalized-odds generalizations were unknown with explicit positioning relative to Alghamdi et al. (2022), Putzel and Lee (2022), Rouzot et al. (2022) and Wang et al. (2024). It also substantially updates limited-information auditing literature and presents binary DCP as prior work by Sabato and Yom-Tov (2020).

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work and closing discussion are extensively rewritten around multiclass auditing. Terminology changes from unfairness/discrepancy to DCP/minDCP, preliminaries are condensed, and greedy and solver derivations move into Appendices C–D. This is substantial narrative restructuring beyond scientific additions and removals.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main text, combines Census and Natality results into shared tables, and relocates numerous retained tables to appendices. It redraws and rearranges the eta plots, removes the binary illustrations and analysis figures, and adds neural-network tables and a convergence figure. These are substantial display changes beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v3 improves multiclass focus, prior-work attribution and neural-network evidence, and supplies useful solver settings. However, v2 Section 9.2.2 explicitly presented unknown-matrix results as upper bounds, whereas v3 claims small upper/lower gaps in both regimes without reporting corresponding minDCP lower-bound values; Table 2 still compares against actual-DCP ranges. The new convergence illustration also substitutes the objective. These gains and stronger, insufficiently supported reliability claims leave the net quality change uncertain.
